The patient presents with acute agitation of ~24-hour duration, without fever, headache, confusion, focal neurologic deficits, or autonomic instability (e.g., tachypnea, hyperthermia, marked hypertension, or diaphoresis). - No reported symptoms suggestive of severe hyponatremia (e.g., nausea, vomiting, lethargy, obtundation, seizures)  

[GAPS]  
- Urine toxicology results (to confirm recent cocaine or MDMA exposure)

- Serum sodium level  
- 12-lead ECG (to assess for stimulant-related arrhythmias, ischemia, or QT prolongation)

Stimulant-induced toxicity (cocaine and/or MDMA)
